title: Judges 11
paragraphs: ¹ Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty warrior, but he was the son of a prostitute. His father was Gilead. ² Gilead's wife also bore him sons, and when those sons grew up they drove Jephthah away. "You will get no inheritance in our father's house," they told him, "because you are the son of another woman." ³ So Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob, where a band of worthless men gathered around him and went out with him. ⁴ Some time later, when the Ammonites made war on Israel, ⁵ the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah back from the land of Tob.

⁶ "Come," they said, "be our commander, so we can fight the Ammonites." ⁷ Jephthah replied to the elders of Gilead, "Didn't you hate me and drive me from my father's house? Why are you coming to me now when you're in trouble?" ⁸ The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "That's exactly why we're turning to you now — come with us to fight the Ammonites, and you will be head over all of us who live in Gilead." ⁹ Jephthah answered them, "If you take me back to fight the Ammonites and the LORD gives them over to me, will I really be your head?" ¹⁰ The elders of Gilead replied, "The LORD is our witness — we will do as you say."

¹¹ So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and commander over them. And Jephthah stated all his terms before the LORD at Mizpah. ¹² Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites, saying, "What do you have against me that you have come to fight against my land?" ¹³ The king of the Ammonites answered Jephthah's messengers, "Because Israel seized my land when they came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and all the way to the Jordan. Now give it back peaceably." ¹⁴ Jephthah sent messengers back to the king of the Ammonites ¹⁵ with this reply: "This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.

¹⁶ When Israel came up from Egypt, they traveled through the wilderness to the Red Sea and then came to Kadesh. ¹⁷ Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Let us pass through your land,' but the king of Edom would not listen. They sent the same request to the king of Moab, who also refused. So Israel stayed at Kadesh. ¹⁸ Then they traveled through the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and Moab. They approached from the east and camped on the other side of the Arnon. They did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was Moab's border. ¹⁹ Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, 'Let us pass through your land to our own place.' ²⁰ But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. He assembled all his troops and camped at Jahaz and fought Israel.

²¹ The LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and his whole army into Israel's hand. Israel defeated them and took possession of all the land of the Amorites who lived in that country. ²² They took over all the Amorite territory from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan. ²³ Since the LORD, the God of Israel, drove out the Amorites before his people Israel, what right do you have to take it over? ²⁴ Take whatever your god Chemosh gives you, and we will take whatever the LORD our God gives us! ²⁵ Are you any better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever quarrel with Israel or go to war against them?

²⁶ Israel has been living in Heshbon and its villages, in Aroer and its villages, and in all the towns along the Arnon for three hundred years. Why haven't you reclaimed them during all that time? ²⁷ I have not wronged you, but you are doing wrong by making war against me. Let the LORD, the Judge, decide the dispute this day between the Israelites and the Ammonites." But the king of the Ammonites ignored Jephthah's message. ²⁹ Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah. He passed through Gilead and Manasseh, through Mizpah in Gilead, and from there crossed over to the Ammonites. ³⁰ And Jephthah made a vow to the LORD: "If you give the Ammonites into my hands,

³¹ then whatever comes out of the door of my house to meet me when I return triumphant from the Ammonites will be the LORD's, and I will sacrifice it as a burnt offering." ³² So Jephthah crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into his hands. ³³ He devastated twenty towns from Aroer to the vicinity of Minnith and all the way to Abel-keramim. Thus Israel subdued Ammon. ³⁴ When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, his daughter came out to meet him, dancing to the sound of tambourines! She was his only child — he had no son or daughter besides her. ³⁵ When he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried, "Oh no, my daughter! You have brought me to my knees! You are one of those who trouble me — for I have given my word to the LORD and I cannot take it back."

³⁶ She replied, "My father, you have given your word to the LORD. Do to me as you promised, now that the LORD has vindicated you against your enemies, the Ammonites." ³⁷ She added, "Grant me this one request. Give me two months to roam the hills and weep with my friends, because I will never marry." ³⁸ "Go," he said. And he let her go for two months. She and her companions went into the hills and wept for her lost future. ³⁹ At the end of two months she returned to her father, and he kept the vow he had made. She had never been with a man. This gave rise to a custom in Israel: ⁴⁰ each year the young women of Israel would go out for four days to commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite.
